cues.en: Tezuka himself, was largely inspired by Disney films like Bambi and Dumbo, and that inspiration wound up leading to the design of large and expressive eyes in his works, that are now commonplace in anime today.

cues.zh: 手冢治虫非常坦率地谈论他的灵感来源以及它如何影响了他的作品，

cues.en: Well once again as it turns out this is not something that Kimba invented.

cues.en: It's not some wildly unique thing that the Lion King wouldn't have come up with, had Kimba not existed.

cues.zh: 有太多这样的比较，让我觉得人们根本不知道什么是常见套路……

cues.zh: 好像这是什么独一无二、只有《森林大帝》才有的东西似的……

cues.en: [Kimba] -You're a real pal.

cues.zh: 我说这些是Kimba粉丝圈常见的批评，真没开玩笑。
cues.en: And I am not kidding when I say that these are common criticisms from the kimba crowd.

cues.zh: 几乎所有讨论这场争议的文章都引用了Fred Patten的一本书，叫《Watching Anime Reading Manga: 25 Years of Essays and Reviews》。
cues.en: Nearly every article that talks about this controversy sources a book from Fred Patten called Watching Anime Reading Manga: 25 Years of Essays and Reviews.

cues.zh: 而在这本书里，能找到我在本期视频中提到的许多离谱对比批评。
cues.en: And within this book can be found many of the insane comparison criticisms that I mentioned in this video.

cues.zh: 包括辛巴有恋爱对象这件事！
cues.en: Including Simba having a love interest!

cues.zh: 不好意思，这在Kimba出现之前早就已经是迪士尼动画电影的标配了！
cues.en: I'm sorry but that was already on the checklist of Disney animated films, well before Kimba ever existed!

cues.zh: 我发誓这真的被收录在他列举相似点的那一节里，而那些相似点看起来已经超出了合理巧合的范畴……
cues.en: And I shit you not this is included in the section where he lists points of similarity which seem to go beyond REASONABLE coincidence...

cues.zh: 这到底算哪门子正当比较啊？！
cues.en: how on earth is that a legitimate comparison?!

cues.zh: 真的感觉这些人根本不知道什么是常见的套路……
cues.en: It legitimately feels as though these people just don't know what common tropes are...

cues.zh: 不过Fred Patten作为动画和漫画爱好者，确实很有可信度：
cues.en: Now Fred Patten actually has a lot of credibility when it comes to being an anime and manga fan:

cues.zh: 他是北美第一个动画粉丝俱乐部的创始成员，被广泛认为是兽迷圈的创始成员之一，还撰写和编辑了许多兽迷书籍，
cues.en: he was a founding member of North America's first anime fan club, he is widely considered to be one of the founding members of the furry fandom and wrote and edited many furry books,

cues.zh: 他在日本动画于美国普及的过程中发挥了巨大作用，这家伙基本上算是最资深的御宅族之一了。
cues.en: he played a gigantic role in popularizing Japanese animation in the United States, this guy was basically like one of the oldest Otaku's.

cues.zh: 他确实留下了相当丰厚的遗产，我想明确表示我的批评不是针对他这个人，我只是非常不同意他对《森林大帝》和《狮子王》的看法。
cues.en: He's actually got quite the legacy and I want to make it clear that my criticisms are not with him as a person, I just really disagree with his take on Kimba and the Lion King.

cues.zh: 有一点需要明白，书是人写的，而人身上满是自己的个人偏见。
cues.en: One thing that needs to be understood is that books are written by human beings and human beings are filled to the brim with their own personal biases.

cues.zh: 不可否认，这家伙显然很喜欢《森林大帝》；但也许这些说法最著名的公开来源，不该出自一个和手冢治虫真的是朋友的人……
cues.en: There's no denying that the guy clearly loved Kimba; but perhaps maybe the most prominent published source for these claims, shouldn't be from a guy who was literally friends with Tezuka...

cues.zh: 你不觉得这可能会稍微影响他对这件事的看法吗？
cues.en: You don't think that might influence his opinion on the matter just a bit?

cues.zh: 他那本书里关于《森林大帝》与辛巴对比的那一章，一开头就说《狮子王》的受欢迎程度普遍归功于其角色和故事的力量：
cues.en: The Kimba versus Simba chapter of his book, starts out by saying that the Lion Kings popularity is generally attributed to the strength of its characters and story:

cues.zh: 狮子王子辛巴从一只缺乏安全感的小狮子，成长为丛林所有动物的强大统治者。
cues.en: the maturing of a lion Prince Simba from an insecure cub, to a strong ruler of all the animals of the jungle.

cues.zh: 接着他说，这个故事出现在动画里并不是第一次，《白狮金巴》讲的就是狮子王子金巴成长的故事，
cues.en: He then goes on to say that this is not the first time that this story has appeared in animation and that Kimba the White Lion is the story of a maturing lion Prince Kimba,

cues.zh: 从一只理想主义却常常天真、自我怀疑的小狮子，成长为丛林所有动物自信的领袖。
cues.en: from an idealistic but often naive cub with self-doubts to a confident leader of all the animals of the jungle.

cues.zh: 当然，我认为《狮子王》成功还有很多其他原因，但大体上，这个总结还算公道。
cues.en: Now I would argue that there are many other reasons why the Lion King was successful, but for the most part this is a fair summary.

cues.zh: 但只有忽略这部剧绝大部分真正内容，这种与《森林大帝》的对比才成立。
cues.en: But this comparison to Kimba only works if you ignore what the vast majority of the show actually is.

cues.zh: 金巴没有逃避责任，也没有他夺回王位合法地位的心路历程，
cues.en: Kimba didn't run away from his responsibilities and there was no arc of him taking his rightful place as king,

cues.zh: 他从一存在就直接统治一切了！
cues.en: He was literally just ruling shit from the moment he started existing!

cues.zh: 所有他统治动物、试图让他们更文明、吃素这些事，都是他小时候干的！
cues.en: All of this shit where he's ruling over the animals, trying to get them to be more civilized and eating vegetarian, is him as a child!

cues.zh: 你不能随便挑系列里金巴碰巧失去信心的片段，就假装这跟角色成长弧线有半点相似。
cues.en: You can't just take random moments from the series, where Kimba happens to lose confidence and pretend it's anything close to resembling a character arc.

cues.zh: 这些对角色毫无增益：它们不过是各自独立剧集里的偶发冲突罢了。
cues.en: They don't add anything to his character: they are literally just incidental conflicts, within contained episodes.

cues.zh: 在Kimba因剧情需要而失去信心的那一集之前的一集里，
cues.en: In the episode previous to one where Kimba would lose confidence as part of the plot,

cues.zh: Kimba和之后的那一集没什么两样！
cues.en: Kimba is no different than the episode after!

cues.zh: 把角色成长弧线所必需的关键情节，拿来跟毫无意义、对剧集毫无影响的填充内容相提并论，是不合理的……
cues.en: It is unreasonable to compare pivotal ideas that are necessary for a characters arc, to random unimportant padding that doesn't change anything about the show...

cues.zh: 虽然你可以说漫画里这个角色有更多发展，
cues.en: And although you could argue that there's more development to this character in the manga,

cues.zh: 但那仍然完全不是一回事！
cues.en: it is still not the same thing at all!

cues.zh: 要想把这两个角色的旅程拿来比较（仿佛它们有什么相似之处），唯一的办法就是把整个体验压缩成一句话。
cues.en: The only way to compare the journey of these two characters (as though they're anything similar) is to reduce the entire experience down to single sentences.

cues.zh: 是啊，如果你无视这两部作品的全部体验，它们听起来确实挺像的。
cues.en: Like yeah, if you ignore the entire experience of both of these properties then they sound pretty similar.

cues.zh: 但这些一句话概括，并不是这两部作品实际体验的样子！
cues.en: But these single sentences are not what the actual experiences of these two properties are!

cues.zh: 现在我还远没有逐一讲完这些说法，但在继续之前，有件事我想先聊聊。
cues.en: Now I'm definitely not done going through each of these claims here, but there's something I want to talk about before I go further.

cues.zh: 当我说要在这场争议中采取反绝对主义的做法时，我确信仍会有很多人无法被说服……
cues.en: When I talk about taking an anti absolutist approach to this controversy, I'm sure that there will still be plenty of people who will not be persuaded...

cues.zh: 我觉得到了某个点，这可能就归结为理念上的差异：我是一个非常支持艺术和创造力的人，
cues.en: And I think after a certain point it might just boil down to a difference in philosophy: I am a very pro art and creativity person,

cues.zh: 正因如此，我反对对艺术和创造力施加限制。
cues.en: and because of that, I am against placing restrictions on art and creativity.

cues.zh: 有很多例子表明，人们创作出了相似的作品，而这些作品彼此完全独立。
cues.en: There are plenty of instances of people creating similar works, that were completely independent from one another.

cues.zh: 这种情况在艺术中确实会发生，尤其是当绝大多数艺术都遵循非常常见的套路和模式时。
cues.en: It is a thing that happens in art especially when the vast majority of art follows very common formulas and tropes.

cues.zh: 我跟你讲，看到人们动不动就指责别人抄袭，我有多沮丧；
cues.en: I cannot tell you how frustrated I get, when people are so quick to accuse others of plagiarism;

cues.zh: 尤其是那些所谓被抄袭的原作，本身压根就没什么原创性……
cues.en: especially when the original works supposedly being copied, is not a very original thing at all...

cues.zh: 绝大多数流行歌曲都是4/4拍。
cues.en: The vast majority of popular songs are in 4/4 time signature.

cues.zh: 绝大多数流行歌曲用的和弦进行，都是听着悦耳的那种。
cues.en: The vast majority of popular songs are going to utilize chord progressions that sound pleasant to the ear.

cues.zh: 你不能随便乱弹和弦，还指望它人人都爱听，什么行得通、什么行不通，是有逻辑公式的。
cues.en: You can't just play random chords and hope that it sounds universally appealing, there is a logical equation to what makes sense and what doesn't.

cues.zh: 我完全能理解一个艺术家的心情——看到一首比自己的歌成功得多、却又和自己的作品有相似之处。
cues.en: And I can fully understand the perspective of an artist that sees a much more successful song, that has similarities to their own.

cues.zh: 他们脑子里总会有一部分觉得，那首更火的歌的成功，本该有自己一份。
cues.en: There's going to be a part of their brain that feels as though they are owed the success of that more popular song.

cues.zh: 但这种感觉不应凌驾于巧合确实存在的事实之上。
cues.en: But that feeling shouldn't trump the reality that coincidence does exist.

cues.zh: 1946年，华纳兄弟发行了一部动画片，兔八哥在钢琴上弹奏《匈牙利狂想曲第二号》，而琴里有一只老鼠。
cues.en: in 1946 Warner Brothers released a cartoon featuring Bugs Bunny playing Hungarian Rhapsody number 2 on the piano, while there was a mouse inside it.

cues.zh: 五个月后，米高梅发行了一部动画片，汤姆猫在钢琴上弹奏《匈牙利狂想曲第二号》，而杰瑞鼠就在琴里。
cues.en: Five months later MGM released a cartoon featuring Tom the cat playing Hungarian Rhapsody number two, on the piano, while Jerry the mouse was inside it.

cues.zh: 虽然不完全相似，但这两部动画片基本上概念完全相同，弹的也是同一首曲子。
cues.en: Although not entirely similar, both of these cartoons have basically the exact same concept and play the exact same song.

cues.zh: *《匈牙利狂想曲第二号》*
cues.en: *Hungarian Rhapsody #2*

cues.zh: [YMS]——这促使两家制片厂互相指责对方抄袭……
cues.en: [YMS] -Which prompted both studios to accuse each other of plagiarism...

cues.zh: 《狂想曲兔子》的上映日期和MPAA审批编号更早，而《猫的协奏曲》的制作编号更靠后，这与同期发行的其他短片情况一致。
cues.en: Now Rhapsody Rabbit had an earlier release date and MPAA approval number, while the Cat Concerto had a more advanced production number, which was consistent with other shorts released around the same time.

cues.zh: 也就是说，这两部电影在上映之前，都已经在制作中了。
cues.en: Meaning both of these films were already in production, before either of them were released.

cues.zh: 那么这种巧合发生的概率到底有多大呢？
cues.en: So what exactly are the odds of this type of coincidence even happening?

cues.zh: 乍一看，唯一合理的结论似乎只能是抄袭，对吧？
cues.en: From first glance, it would appear as though the only reasonable conclusion would have to be plagiarism, right?

cues.zh: 但仔细想想，其实这事并没有看起来那么不可能。
cues.en: Well if you think about it it's actually not as unlikely as it seems.

cues.zh: 当你开始拆解这两部电影的概念时，就会发现它并没有那么独特或原创。
cues.en: When you start to break down the concept of these two films, you start to realize that it's not all that wildly unique or original.

cues.zh: 用古典音乐和其他公有领域音乐作为动画概念的基础，绝对不是什么闻所未闻的事。
cues.en: It was definitely not unheard of to use classical and other public domain music, as the foundation for animation concepts.

cues.zh: 熟悉《乐一通》的人早就知道这一点。
cues.en: Anyone familiar with Looney Tunes would already know this.

cues.zh: *《蓝色多瑙河圆舞曲》响起*
cues.en: *Blue Danube Waltz playing*

cues.zh: [YMS]——虽然米高梅不像华纳兄弟那样频繁使用这种做法，但早在1932年就有他们这样做的例子了。
cues.en: [YMS] -And although MGM didn't do this as frequently as Warner Brothers, there are still examples of them doing this as early as 1932.

cues.zh: 这种概念早在上述两部电影之前就已存在。
cues.en: This type of concept existed well before either of these two films.

cues.zh: 如果有人觉得《匈牙利狂想曲第二号》那种充满活力的基调很适合做成动画，
cues.en: And if someone were to decide that the energetic tone of Hungarian Rhapsody #2 would lend itself well to animation,

cues.zh: 那么他们接着决定让一个角色弹钢琴，就完全合情合理，因为这本来就是一首钢琴曲……🤔
cues.en: It is entirely reasonable that they would then decide to have a character playing a piano, since it is a song on the piano...🤔

cues.zh: 而且动画短片里出现拟人化动物角色也非常常见，
cues.en: And since it's also incredibly common for animated shorts to feature anthropomorphic animal characters,

cues.zh: 所以他们接着决定用一只老鼠来制造冲突，就完全合情合理。
cues.en: it is entirely reasonable that they would then decide to use a mouse for the conflict.

cues.zh: 至于这些短片里实际出现的笑料，大多数都不一样。
cues.en: Now in terms of the actual gags that appear in these shorts, the majority of them are different.

cues.zh: 但这起争议之所以有意思，是因为你完全可以有理由地说，两者提供的体验大体相同；
cues.en: But what makes this particular controversy interesting, is that you can reasonably argue that they're both offering, more or less, the same experience;

cues.zh: 而这一点，你可没法套用在《狮子王》和《森林大帝》上！
cues.en: which is not something you can say for The Lion King and Kimba!

cues.zh: 我想先说清楚，我并不是在说抄袭他人想法的情况不存在。
cues.en: I want to be clear, that I am NOT suggesting that ripping off other people's ideas doesn't exist.

cues.zh: 而且就算是我举的那些例子，也完全有可能是抄袭，而非巧合。
cues.en: And even with the examples I've presented, it's still entirely possible that these were the result of plagiarism, rather than coincidence.

cues.zh: 但当我提到理念上的差异时，我的意思是：我不愿意贸然
cues.en: But when I mention difference in philosophy, what I mean is: that I am not comfortable jumping to

cues.zh: 对版权侵权下结论，前提是能够合理假设，所涉及的两个作品本可以各自独立创作出来。
cues.en: conclusions about copyright infringement, if it can be reasonably assumed that the two properties in question, could have been created independently from each other.

cues.zh: 尤其是当我们谈论的图像、概念和主题，本来就没那么独特的时候，
cues.en: and especially if we're talking about images, concepts and themes that were never really all that unique in the first place,

cues.zh: 艺术中已有的那些公式和套路，会让这类巧合发生的可能性远比你想象的要高。
cues.en: the formulas and tropes that already exist within art, make these types of coincidences a lot more likely than you would think.

cues.zh: 就算你觉得这种事发生的概率只有千分之一，但你猜怎么着，
cues.en: Even if you think there's a one in a thousand chance of something like this happening, well guess what,

cues.zh: 外面至少有数以百万计的知识产权。
cues.en: There's at least millions of intellectual properties out there.

cues.zh: 在我看来，从统计上讲这是不可避免的。
cues.en: To me it seems statistically inevitable.

cues.zh: 考虑到我们只有在涉及的作品之一大获成功时才会听说这些巧合，
cues.en: And considering that we only ever hear about these coincidences when one of the properties in question is massively successful,

cues.zh: 这种事发生的频率很可能比我们意识到的要高得多。
cues.en: It is likely happening a lot more often than we realize.

cues.zh: 《狮子王》之所以是现在这个样子，有非常合乎逻辑的原因，而这些原因完全独立于《森林大帝》存在。
cues.en: There are very logical reasons why the Lion King is the way it is, and these reasons exist completely independently of Kimba.

cues.zh: 这场争议真正让我恼火的是，《森林大帝》的拥护者喜欢宣称对早在《森林大帝》之前就已存在的概念拥有所有权。
cues.en: Something that really irks me about this controversy, is that the Kimba crowd likes to claim ownership over ideas that existed well before Kimba.

cues.zh: 《狮子王》的创作者非常坦率地承认从莎士比亚的《哈姆雷特》中汲取了灵感（顺便说一句，那是公有领域作品）
cues.en: The creators of the Lion King were very open about taking inspiration from Shakespeare's Hamlet (which by the way, is public domain)

cues.zh: 然而尽管如此，他们仍然假装《狮子王》一定是因为这些相同的概念而抄袭了《森林大帝》。
cues.en: and yet despite that, they still pretend as though the Lion King must have ripped off Kimba for these same concepts.

cues.zh: 王室、被谋杀的国王，以及试图夺回王位的儿子的设定。
cues.en: The idea of royalty and a king who was murdered and his son who tries to claim his rightful place in the throne.

cues.zh: 正如我已经提到的，Kimba其实从来不需要夺回他的王位；
cues.en: As I've already mentioned, Kimba never really had to reclaim his place as king;

cues.zh: 而且，Claude并没有杀害他的父亲，甚至和他毫无血缘关系。
cues.en: and on top of that, Claude didn't kill his father and he's not even related to him.

cues.zh: 他其实就是一只随便的混蛋狮子，任何持相反说法的文章显然都没看过Kimba！
cues.en: He is literally just some random asshole lion and any article claiming otherwise clearly hasn't watched Kimba!

cues.zh: 非常明显，这些设定与《狮子王》和《哈姆雷特》之间的契合度，远远高于与Kimba的契合度。
cues.en: It is so incredibly clear, that these ideas fit so much more closely between The Lion King and Hamlet, than they do with Kimba.

cues.zh: 那么，你到底怎么能说Kimba是《狮子王》中这些设定的来源呢？
cues.en: So, how on earth can you claim that Kimba is responsible for these ideas appearing in the Lion King?

cues.zh: 甚至主角看到亡父显灵这一概念，也来自《哈姆雷特》。
cues.en: Even the concept of the main character seeing his dead father as an apparition, was from Hamlet.

cues.en: Hamlet also runs through trees in the dark before this happens; and the very last thing the King says before he disappears, is also, remarkably similar to The Lion King.

cues.en: [YMS] -So, since the Lion King very clearly used Hamlet as an inspiration for this, then the criticism from the Kimba crowd, should be limited to just purely visual aesthetics, right?

cues.en: What the Kimba crowd doesn't tell you, is that there are dozens of examples throughout these series, of characters being hallucinated by others.

cues.en: Kimba sees his dead mom in the water and then the stars, he also sees his mom in a music box, Kimba sees his dad in a moon...?

cues.en: At one point, he just shows up right over top of him...

cues.en: There's another point where Kimba just tf's into his dad for a second...

cues.en: We see his dad in the snow and the lightning and sometimes just right in front of him.

cues.zh: 这样的场景还挺多的，而且不只限于 Kimba 和他的父母。
cues.en: There are quite a few of these, and they're not even limited to just Kimba and his parents.

cues.en: Fucking Roger hallucinated at his uncle in the clouds...

cues.en: You got Kimba's friend Speedy hallucinating Kimba as a bubble,

cues.en: you got Kimba hallucinating his friends, just running around in the forest,

cues.en: you got some boy hallucinating Kimba in the clouds,

cues.en: you got Kitty hallucinating her mom in purgatory or some shit,

cues.en: you got Kimba hallucinating the woolly mammoth character...

cues.en: Given just how many different ways they've shown characters hallucinating other characters, how on earth was the Lion King supposed to be able to replicate the dead father apparition from Hamlet,

cues.en: without doing something that looks similar to what Kimba has already done?

cues.en: But even if he did show up as a constellation, that is not something that Kimba invented!

cues.en: Do you not know what constellations are?!

cues.en: Now granted, there is one image out of the dozens of hallucinations from Kimba, showing his dad appearing in the clouds.

cues.zh: 这出自1991年那部无对白的交响诗版《森林大帝》电影。
cues.en: This is from the 1991 symphonic poem Kimba film, with no dialogue.

cues.zh: 基本上，这是一部直接发行视频的剧情概要，讲述的是Kimba非常早期的事件；这是影片的最后一个镜头，他正游回丛林，就在逃离船只之后。
cues.en: Basically, it's a straight-to-video summary, of the very early events of Kimba; and this is the last shot of the film, where he's swimming back to the jungle, right after escaping the boat.

cues.zh: 他的父亲没有与他交流，也没有暗示说你应该按字面理解这个画面；这是一种视觉美学选择，用来结束影片，实际上它参考了漫画的最后一页。
cues.en: His father doesn't communicate to him and there's no implication that you're supposed to take this image literally; it is a visual aesthetic choice to end the film on, and it's actually a reference to the last page of the manga.

cues.zh: 现在《狮子王》早在1991年这部直接发行视频的影片在日本上映之前就已经进入制作阶段，但漫画显然在这之前就已经存在了。
cues.en: Now The Lion King was already well into production before this 1991 straight-to-video film came out in Japan, but the manga obviously existed well before this.

cues.zh: 不出所料，有许多人用这个画面作为证据，证明《狮子王》抄袭了Kimba；但他们没有告诉你的是，这朵云根本不是Kimba的父亲……
cues.en: Unsurprisingly, there are many that used this panel as evidence that the Lion King ripped off Kimba; but what they don't tell you, is that this cloud is not kimba's dad at all...

cues.zh: 云朵其实就是Kimba，下面的小狮子是Kimba的儿子。
cues.en: The cloud is literally kimba and the lion cub below is kimba's son.

cues.zh: 这是漫画结尾处，那时Kimba已经长大了；剧透一下，Kimba死了……
cues.en: This is at the very end of the manga once Kimba has already grown up; and spoilers, Kimba dies...

cues.zh: 再说一次，这只是漫画结尾的一种视觉美学选择，不应按字面理解。
cues.en: Once again, this is a visual aesthetic choice to end the manga on, and it's not meant to be taken literally.

cues.zh: 这并不是出自狮子出现在云中与儿子交流的场景。
cues.en: This is not from a scene where a lion shows up in the clouds, to communicate with their son.

cues.zh: 1966年的续集系列结尾也引用了这个画面；但在这个系列中，他们改动了漫画的故事，所以Kimba最后没有死……
cues.en: They also referenced this panel at the end of the sequel series in 1966; but in this series, they changed the story from the manga, so that Kimba doesn't die at the end...

cues.zh: 所以没错，这只狮子其实并不代表任何人，只是用来结束系列的一种视觉美学选择。
cues.en: So yeah, this lion isn't really supposed to be anyone and it's just a visual aesthetic choice, to end the series on.

cues.zh: 无论你拿这个画面的哪个版本来和《狮子王》比较，
cues.en: Regardless of which instance of this image you compare to the Lion King,

cues.zh: 这个画面的背景都完全不同，《狮子王》也绝没有在视觉或其他方面试图复制它。
cues.en: there is a completely different context to this image and the Lion King was in no way trying to replicate it, visually or otherwise.

cues.zh: 《狮子王》的创作者们曾反复琢磨过许多不同的创意，最后才决定让父亲在云中出现，
cues.en: The creators of the Lion King floated around many different ideas, before deciding to have his father show up in the clouds,

cues.en: and somehow these concept images alone, are used as evidence that they're ripping off Kimba??

cues.zh: 不好意思，你是不了解电影是怎么制作的吗？？
cues.en: I'm sorry, but do you not understand how films are made??

cues.zh: 像这样的大制片厂作品，必然会经历好几个不同的概念阶段，来琢磨如何传达他们的想法。
cues.en: A big studio production like this, is bound to go through several different concepts for how they want to communicate their ideas.

cues.zh: 这是一个协作的过程，大家互相交流碰撞想法，最后才定下最好的那个。
cues.en: It is a collaborative effort, where people bounce ideas off of each other, before deciding on the best one.

cues.zh: 我是说，看看沙祖以前长什么样就知道了……
cues.en: I mean, just look at what Zazu used to look like...

cues.zh: 首先，《森林大帝》并没有发明白狮子；其次，把你抄袭的指控延伸到根本没出现在电影里的概念图上，这怎么说得通？
cues.en: First of all, Kimba did not invent white lions; and second, how does it make any sense to stretch your accusations of plagiarism, to concepts that didn't even appear in the film?

cues.en: If having a white lion as one of the many different potential design concepts,

cues.en: is somehow evidence that Disney was ripping off Kimba from the very beginning,

cues.en: Who is the black lion cub supposed to be?

cues.en: There's concept images of Scar without even having a scar.

cues.en: Initially, his character was supposed to be king of the baboons.

cues.en: [Clip] -I was handed this treatment, it was sort of a war between lions and Baboons.

cues.en: Rafiki was a cheetah, the character of scar was actually the leader of the baboons.

cues.en: So a very different tale.

cues.en: Now the hyenas and scar and some other characters are ones that I've still yet to properly address in this video,

cues.zh: 但既然显然日本以外几乎没有人真正看过《森林大帝》，我觉得有必要先让你们了解一下这些节目实际上是什么样的。
cues.en: but since apparently pretty much nobody outside of Japan has actually seen Kimba, I feel it's important to first give you an idea of what each of these shows are actually like.

cues.zh: 在没有真正看过《森林大帝》的情况下对这场争议持有强烈意见的最大问题是，你的大脑会随意填补它想要的内容。
cues.en: The biggest problem with having strong opinions on this controversy, without actually having seen Kimba, is that your mind fills in whatever it wants to.

cues.zh: 当你把两张看起来相似的图片并排放置，而你只熟悉其中一张的背景时，你的大脑会自动假设你不熟悉的那张也有相似的背景。
cues.en: When you have two similar looking images side-by-side and you're familiar only with the context of one of them, your brain automatically assumes that there is a similar context to the one you're unfamiliar with.

cues.en: your brain assumes that there must have been some sort of Pride Rock equivalency in Kimba.

cues.en: In reality the Kimba characters did not live on a Pride Rock equivalency.

cues.en: Kimba basically just had a hut in the jungle made out of spiky vines, where he lived with his dead dad's body.

cues.zh: 在续集系列里他住在一棵树里面，而在89版系列里他住在一架坠毁的飞机里。
cues.en: In the sequel series he lived inside of a tree, and in the 89 series he lived in a crashed airplane.

cues.zh: 并没有一个反复出现的悬崖场景可以称得上与荣耀石相似。
cues.en: There is no recurring cliff location that one could say is similar to Pride Rock.

cues.zh: 任何角色站在悬崖边的镜头都纯粹是为了美观而偶然出现的。
cues.en: And any shot of the characters on the edge of a cliff is purely incidental for aesthetic purposes.

cues.zh: 这些时刻通常出现在一集结尾，用来营造规模感和收尾感。
cues.en: These moments usually took place at the end of an episode to give a sense of scale and closure.

cues.zh: 但真正看过这部剧之后就会发现，这些角色对比只有在把角色本身的一切特质都剥离掉之后才成立。
cues.en: But, after actually having watched the show it becomes pretty clear that these character comparisons only work if you strip away everything that the character actually is.

cues.zh: 先从波莉和沙祖说起。
cues.en: Let's start with Polly and Zazu.

cues.zh: 如果你只看过《森林大帝》粉丝做的视频，没真正看过这部剧，
cues.en: Now, if you've only seen videos from the Kimba crowd and haven't actually watched the show,

cues.zh: 你大概会以为波莉有点像总管管家型的角色，跟沙祖差不多。
cues.en: you'd probably assume that Polly is kind of like a head servant majordomo type character, like Zazu.

cues.zh: 然而事实证明，这并不正确。
cues.en: Well, as it turns out that NOT TRUE.

cues.zh: 当然，他是主要角色之一，而且也是只鸟，但除了这两个极其简化的相似点之外，这两个角色完全不同。
cues.en: Like, sure he's in the main cast of characters and he's also a bird, but beyond those two incredibly reductive similarities these are not the same characters at all.

cues.zh: Polly Cracker就是个愚蠢的搞笑担当鸟，整天都在生气。
cues.en: Polly Cracker is literally just a dumb comic relief bird who gets angry all the time.

cues.en: What defines Zazu as a character is that he has a strong sense of responsibility and tradition and order.

cues.zh: 他履行皇家助手的职责，并尽力避免任何冲突。
cues.en: He fulfills his role as a royal assistant and tries his best to avoid conflict at every turn.

cues.en: Whereas Polly is just a dumb bird with anger problems...

cues.zh: 毫不夸张地说，Polly最核心的性格特征就是他整天生气、总想打架。
cues.en: Without any exaggeration the most defining character trait of Polly is that he's angry and wants to fight all the time.
